title: Cultivation of Mammalian Cells Using a Single-use Pneumatic Bioreactor System
protocol: Login to the Bioreactor system.
Select user name and enter password.
Click "Login".
Inspect pH sensor to ensure tip is filled with electrolyte solution.
Prepare two beakers with pH calibration solutions (pH 4 and pH 7).
Connect the pH cable to the pH sensor.
Navigate to the “Actions” tab on the Hello interface.
Click “calibrate” under Actions.
Enter buffer temperature in Calibration Solution Temp field.
Place pH sensor in buffer 1 (pH 4) and enter value in the “zero” field.
Wait for graph to stabilize, then click the “calibrate 1” button.
Rinse the pH sensor with distilled water.
Place sensor in buffer 2 (pH 7).
Enter buffer 2 value in the “span” field.
Wait for graph to stabilize and click "Calibrate 2" button.
Click “Save”, then click “Close”.
Ensure DO sensor has been polarized by being connected to the system for several hours.
Navigate to the “Actions” tab on the Hello interface.
Click calibrate under Actions.
Click the “DO A” button.
Disconnect the DO sensor and enter 0 in the “zero” field.
Wait for graph to stabilize, then click the “Calibrate 1” button.
Reconnect the DO sensor and enter 100 in the “Span” field.
Wait for graph to stabilize and click "Calibrate 2" button.
Click “Save”, then click “Close”.
Autoclave sensors and thermal well for 30 min at 121 °C, 15 psi.
Sanitize autoclaved pouches with 70% Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA).
Transfer sanitized pouches to biological safety cabinet (BSC).
Remove outer packaging of vessel in BSC.
Sanitize inner packaging with 70% IPA.
Inspect the vessel and tubing for damage.
Install pH sensors in two front ports of the vessel.
Install DO sensors in corresponding ports tightly.
Thread sensors into ports securely.
Transfer vessel out of BSC.
Hang DO and pH sensor cables outside the vessel sleeve.
Slide the vessel into the sleeve feet first.
Fit temperature sensor into the vessel thermal well carefully.
Ensure bottom of the vessel rests against the heaters.
Remove tubing sets from their bags.
Match color coding on tubing to corresponding connectors and pumps.
Install main gas line by pressing connector into its outlet.
Twist micro gas line connector clockwise into gas outlet.
Open filter oven.
Secure exhaust filter on U-channel so tubing goes through hooks.
Connect tubing out of oven.
Install the tubing by condenser bag in the tubing holder.
Close the door.
Route addition lines A and B, both media lines, and the harvest line behind the DO sensor and onto the bench next to the bioreactor control unit.
Connect the cables to the DO and pH sensors.
Navigate to the “actions” tab and click “Control Pumps” on the computer interface.
Form a sterile connection between an unused medium addition line (1 orange band) and the medium bottle/bag source by welding the tubing or using Luer fittings.
Click the slider to turn on the media pump on.
Click the slider to turn the media pump off after adding the desired amount of medium.
Place microcarrier beads in Ca2+, Mg2+ free PBS for 3 hr at RT.
Wash beads several times with Ca2+, Mg2+ free PBS.
Autoclave for 15 min at 115 °C, 15 psi.
Add 3 g/L (dry weight) of micro-carriers in this experiment.
Pump in micro-carriers that have been hydrated, washed and autoclaved into the reactor in the same manner the medium was added in step 4.1.
Set the controllers to Auto and enter the desired setpoints.
Here, use Agitation Set Point (SP) = 15 rpm, Temperature SP = 37.0 °C, pH = 7.2, DO = 100%.
Wait for the parameters to equilibrate.
Confirm sensor is fully polarized.
Confirm DO present value has stabilized.
Navigate to the “Actions” tab and click “calibrate”.
Click “DO A”, click “One-point”.
Enter ‘100’ in the “Span” field.
Click the “Calibrate 1” button.
Click “Save.”
Click “close.”
Navigate to the Actions tab.
Click “Batch.”
Use the on-screen keyboard or an external keyboard to enter a batch name 16 characters or less.
Click the on-screen keyboard’s “Hide” button.
Click the “Start batch” button.
Confirm by clicking “Start” in the overlay.
Form a sterile connection between an unused medium addition line and the cell bottle/bag source.
Install the silicone section of the tubing in the media pump so the arrow points toward the tubing between the pump and vessel.
Check that the tubing clamp is open and its branched tubing clamp is closed.
Click the slider to turn the media pump on.
Click to “Off” after adding cells.
Navigate to the “Actions” tab.
Click “Control Pumps.”
Navigate to the “actions” tab.
Click “take sample.”
Place the sampling tubing in the sampling pump.
Manipulate the sampling stopcock according to the on-screen instructions.
Perform at least a daily microscopic observation and cell count on these samples.
Infect the cells with the addition of a virus inoculum when they have reached 1.2 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Aseptically add the inoculum to a 20 ml syringe.
Connect the syringe to one of the spare addition ports on the reactor.
Introduce the inoculum to the reactor by pressing on the syringe plunger.
Continue sampling and analyzing the culture for adenovirus intracellular particle concentration.
